drivingQuestion: If Rabbi Akiva conceded to Rabbi Yeshevav that a severed windpipe renders the animal an unslaughtered carcass, how can the mishna of Elu Tereifot list a severed windpipe among the tereifot?
outcomeNote: The contradiction is settled by Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba in Rabbi Yoḥanan's name (before/after Rabbi Akiva's retraction), Rava's and Reish Lakish's resolutions having been pressed. The coda leaves Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov's Jew/gentile distinction standing against a baraita taught expressly not like him.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט וְכוּ׳. וְהוֹדָה לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא. וּרְמִינְהִי: אֵלּוּ טְרֵפוֹת בַּבְּהֵמָה
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna teaches: If «one cut the gullet…and Rabbi Akiva conceded to his» opinion. «And» the Gemara «raises a contradiction» from a mishna at the beginning of the next chapter (42a): «These» wounds constitute «tereifot in an animal:»

segments.he: נְקוּבַת הַוֶּושֶׁט וּפְסוּקַת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת!
segments.en: An animal that has «a perforated gullet,» where the perforation goes through the wall of the gullet, «or» one with «a severed windpipe.» According to this mishna, the severed windpipe renders the animal a tereifa and not an unslaughtered carcass. If Rabbi Akiva reconsidered his opinion and conceded to Rabbi Yeshevav, in accordance with the opinion of which tanna is that mishna?

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן שֶׁשָּׁחַט וּלְבַסּוֹף פָּסַק, כָּאן שֶׁפָּסַק וּלְבַסּוֹף שָׁחַט. שָׁחַט וּלְבַסּוֹף פָּסַק – נִפְסֶלֶת בִּשְׁחִיטָה הִיא, פָּסַק וּלְבַסּוֹף שָׁחַט – כִּי דָּבָר אַחֵר גָּרַם לָהּ לִיפָּסֵל דָּמְיָא.
segments.en: «Rava said:» This is «not difficult. Here,» the mishna is referring to a case «where one cut» the gullet «and ultimately severed» the windpipe not in the standard manner. «There,» the mishna in the next chapter is referring to a case «where he severed» the windpipe not in the standard manner, «and ultimately cut» the gullet. If he «cut» the gullet «and ultimately severed» the windpipe, the animal «was rendered unfit during its slaughter;» therefore, it assumes the status of an unslaughtered carcass, according to the principle of Rabbi Yeshevav. But if «he severed» the windpipe «and ultimately cut» the gullet, it is «as» though «another matter caused» the animal «to become unfit;» therefore, it assumes the status of a tereifa.

segments.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא לְרָבָא: שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט וּפָסַק אֶת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת, פָּסַק אֶת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט – נְבֵלָה!
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa bar Huna raised an objection to Rava» from a baraita: If one «cut the gullet and» then «severed the windpipe,» or if one «severed the windpipe and cut the gullet thereafter,» the animal is «an unslaughtered carcass.» Apparently, contrary to Rava’s statement, the order is irrelevant, and even if the windpipe is severed first, the animal assumes the status of an unslaughtered carcass.

segments.he: אֵימָא: וּכְבָר שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט מֵעִיקָּרָא.
segments.en: Rava said: «Say» that the latter case in the baraita means not that he cut the gullet thereafter; rather, it is a case where one severed the windpipe «and had already cut the gullet at the outset.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁתֵּי תְּשׁוּבוֹת בַּדָּבָר, חֲדָא דְּהַיְינוּ קַמַּיְיתָא, וְעוֹד הָא תְּנַן ״וְאַחַר כָּךְ״!
segments.en: Rav Aḥa bar Huna «said to him:» There are «two refutations of the statement,» i.e., of your attempt to answer the difficulty from the baraita: «One» is that if the second case in the baraita is one where he initially cut the gullet, then «that is» identical to «the first» case in the baraita. «And furthermore, didn’t we learn» explicitly in the baraita: Or if one severed the windpipe and cut the gullet «thereafter,» the animal is an unslaughtered carcass?

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אֵלּוּ אֲסוּרוֹת קָתָנֵי, וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶן נְבֵלוֹת, וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶן טְרֵפוֹת.
segments.en: «Rather, Rava said:» The use of the term: Tereifot, in the mishna in the next chapter is not to the exclusion of unslaughtered carcasses; rather, the tanna «teaches» that term in a general sense, meaning: «These» wounds serve to render an animal «forbidden; and there are» some «of them» that are «unslaughtered carcasses,» e.g., an animal with a severed windpipe, «and there are» some «of them» that are «tereifot.»

segments.he: וְלִיחְשׁוֹב נָמֵי דְּחִזְקִיָּה, דְּאָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: עֲשָׂאָהּ גִּיסְטְרָא – נְבֵלָה, וְלִיחְשׁוֹב נָמֵי דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: נִטְּלָה יָרֵךְ וְחָלָל שֶׁלָּהּ – נְבֵלָה.
segments.en: The Gemara objects to that interpretation: If the mishna is listing those circumstances that render the animal an unslaughtered carcass, «let» the tanna «consider» the circumstance «of Ḥizkiyya as well, as Ḥizkiyya says:» If «one rendered» the animal like «a shard» by cutting it into two widthwise, its halakhic status is that of «an unslaughtered carcass» even while it is convulsing before its death. «And let» the tanna «consider» the circumstance «of Rabbi Elazar as well, as Rabbi Elazar said:» If «the thigh,» the hind leg of the animal, «was removed and its recess» is obvious (see 21a), it is «an unslaughtered carcass.»

segments.he: כִּי קָתָנֵי נְבֵלָה, דְּלָא מְטַמְּאָה מֵחַיִּים, אֲבָל נְבֵלָה דִּמְטַמְּאָה מֵחַיִּים – לָא קָתָנֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara explains: «When» the mishna «teaches» the case of «an unslaughtered carcass,» it is a case where the animal «does not» assume that status and «impart impurity while alive. But» the tanna «does not teach» the case of «an unslaughtered carcass» where the animal assumes that status and «imparts impurity while alive,» e.g., the cases of Ḥizkiyya and Rabbi Elazar.

segments.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כָּאן – שֶׁשָּׁחַט בִּמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ, כָּאן – שֶׁשָּׁחַט שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ. שָׁחַט בִּמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ – נִפְסְלָה בִּשְׁחִיטָה הִיא, שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ – כִּי דָּבָר אַחֵר גָּרַם לָהּ לִיפָּסֵל דָּמְיָא.
segments.en: «Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish» resolved the apparent contradiction between the mishna here and the mishna on 42a, and «said: Here,» the tanna is referring to a case «where one cut» the gullet «in» the same «place» as the initial «cut» in the windpipe. «There,» on 42a, the tanna is referring to a case «where he cut» the gullet «not in» the same «place» as the initial «cut» in the windpipe. The reason for the distinction is that if «one cut» the gullet «in» the same «place» as the initial «cut» in the windpipe, it is an animal that «was rendered unfit during its slaughter» and it assumes the status of an unslaughtered carcass. By contrast, if he cut the gullet «not in» the same «place» as the initial «cut» in the windpipe it is «like» a case where «another matter caused» the animal «to become unfit.» Therefore, cutting the gullet renders it a tereifa and prevents it from imparting ritual impurity.

segments.he: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: שָׁחַט אֶת הַקָּנֶה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִיקְּבָה הָרֵיאָה כְּשֵׁרָה! אַלְמָא כְּמַאן דְּמַנְּחָא בְּדִיקּוּלָא דָּמְיָא, הָכָא נָמֵי כְּמַאן דְּמַנְּחָא בְּדִיקּוּלָא דָּמְיָא.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And did Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish say this,» that slaughter can be effective to prevent impurity after the windpipe was severed? «But doesn’t Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish say:» If one «cut the windpipe and the lung was perforated thereafter» before he cut the gullet, the animal is «fit» for consumption? «Apparently,» after cutting the windpipe, the status of the lungs, whose existence is dependent upon the windpipe, «is like» that of an item «that is placed in a basket;» they are irrelevant to the determination of the animal’s status. «Here too,» when the windpipe is severed at the beginning of the slaughter the windpipe should be considered «like» an item «that is placed in a basket» in the sense that the animal is considered to have only one siman, the gullet, and cutting of one siman does not affect the animal’s status.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן קוֹדֶם חֲזָרָה, כָּאן לְאַחַר חֲזָרָה, וּמִשְׁנָה לֹא זָזָה מִמְּקוֹמָהּ.
segments.en: «Rather, Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» The apparent contradiction is «not difficult. There» (42a), where it is stated that an animal with a severed windpipe is a tereifa, the mishna presents the opinion of Rabbi Akiva «before retraction» of his opinion. «Here,» the mishna presents the opinion of Rabbi Akiva «after retraction» of his opinion. «And» even though Rabbi Akiva retracted his opinion, «a mishna does not move from its place.» Once this version of the mishna was learned in the study hall, it remained valuable, even though it is no longer current.

segments.he: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: שָׁחַט אֶת הַקָּנֶה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִיקְּבָה הָרֵיאָה – כְּשֵׁרָה. אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אֶלָּא בְּרֵיאָה, הוֹאִיל וְחַיֵּי רֵיאָה תְּלוּיִן בַּקָּנֶה, אֲבָל בִּבְנֵי מֵעַיִים – לָא.
segments.en: § The Gemara discusses «the» matter «itself» that was cited previously. «Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:» If one «cut the windpipe and the lung was perforated thereafter» before he cut the gullet, the animal is «fit» for consumption. «Rava said: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish states» this principle «only with regard to a lung, since the function of the lung is dependent upon the windpipe.» Once the windpipe is severed it is as though the lungs were removed from the animal. «But with regard to innards» that were perforated after the windpipe was cut but before the slaughter was completed, «no,» the animal becomes a tereifa, because the function of the innards is not dependent on the windpipe.

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: מֵאַחַר שֶׁנּוֹלְדוּ בָּהּ סִימָנֵי טְרֵפָה הִתַּרְתָּ, מָה לִי בְּרֵיאָה, מָה לִי בִּבְנֵי מֵעַיִים!
segments.en: «Rabbi Zeira objects to» Rava’s distinction. «Since» when «signs of being a tereifa developed» in the animal after the slaughter began, «you permitted» the animal and deemed the slaughter valid, «what» difference is there «to me» if the perforation was «in» the «lung,» and «what» difference is there «to me» if the perforation was «in» the «innards?» In either case, the animal should not be deemed a tereifa if the signs developed once the slaughter began.

segments.he: וַהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא, דְּבָעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא: נִיקְּבוּ בְּנֵי מֵעַיִים בֵּין סִימָן לְסִימָן, מַהוּ? מִי מִצְטָרֵף סִימָן רִאשׁוֹן לְסִימָן שֵׁנִי לְטַהֲרָהּ מִידֵי נְבֵלָה, אוֹ לָא?
segments.en: «But Rabbi Zeira retracted» his objection, «as Rabbi Zeira raises a dilemma:» If the «innards were perforated between» the cutting of the first «siman and» the second «siman what is» the halakha? «Does the first siman join» together «with the second siman to purify» the animal «from» the impurity of «an unslaughtered carcass or not?»

segments.he: וְאָמְרִינַן: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּבָעֵי אִילְפָא: הוֹצִיא עוּבָּר אֶת יָדוֹ בֵּין סִימָן לְסִימָן, מַהוּ?
segments.en: «And we say: Isn’t this» the «dilemma that Ilfa raises: If a fetus extended its foreleg» outside the womb while the mother was being slaughtered, «between» the cutting of the first «siman,» the windpipe, and the second «siman,» the gullet, thereby causing the foreleg to have the status of a tereifa, «what is» the halakha?

segments.he: מִי מִצְטָרֵף סִימָן רִאשׁוֹן לְסִימָן שֵׁנִי לְטַהֲרָהּ מִידֵי נְבֵלָה, אוֹ לָא?
segments.en: The Gemara clarifies this dilemma: «Does the first siman join» together «with the second siman to purify the animal from» the impurity of «an unslaughtered carcass or not?» In both cases the dilemma is: Does the cutting of the first siman, which serves the dual purpose of being a component of permitting consumption and preventing impurity of the animal, join together with the cutting of the second siman, which serves only the purpose of preventing impurity, in order to constitute a single act of slaughter and thereby prevent the animal from assuming the impurity of an unslaughtered carcass? Or perhaps because the cutting of each siman is performed for a different purpose they do not join together?

segments.he: עַד כָּאן לָא אִיבַּעְיָא לַן, אֶלָּא לְטַהֲרָהּ מִידֵי נְבֵלָה, אֲבָל בַּאֲכִילָה – אֲסוּרָה.
segments.en: In any event, «we raise the dilemma only» in order «to purify» the foreleg «from» the impurity of «an unslaughtered carcass. But with regard to eating» the slaughtered animal, all agree that it is «forbidden,» as even Rabbi Zeira concedes that the animal is a tereifa and retracts his objection to the distinction that Rava proposed between the lungs and the innards.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב לְרָבִינָא: דִּלְמָא לְעוֹלָם לָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ, וְרַבִּי זֵירָא לִדְבָרָיו דְּרָבָא קָאָמַר, וְלֵיהּ לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Rav Aḥa bar Rav said to Ravina: Perhaps» Rabbi Zeira «actually did not retract» his opinion, as even initially he held that there is no distinction between lungs and innards. If either is perforated after one siman was cut, the animal is a tereifa. «And Rabbi Zeira stated» his objection to the distinction of Rava «in accordance with the statement of Rava, but» he «himself does not hold accordingly.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, מְזַמְּנִין יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל בְּנֵי מֵעַיִין, וְאֵין מְזַמְּנִין גּוֹי עַל בְּנֵי מֵעַיִין.
segments.en: The Gemara continues its analysis of the statement of Reish Lakish, who said that after the windpipe is cut, the lung is considered as though it was placed in a basket, and if it is perforated before the slaughter is completed, the animal does not become a tereifa. «Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov said: Learn from» the statement «of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish» that «one may invite Jews» to eat the «innards» of an animal that was slaughtered, «but one may not invite gentiles» to eat the «innards» of an animal that was slaughtered, because they are forbidden to gentiles.

segments.he: מַאי טַעְמָא? יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּבִשְׁחִיטָה תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא, כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא שְׁחִיטָה מְעַלַּיְיתָא – אִישְׁתְּרִי לְהוּ; גּוֹיִם דְּבִנְחִירָה סַגִּי לְהוּ וּבְמִיתָה תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא, הָנֵי – כְּאֵבֶר מִן הַחַי דָּמוּ.
segments.en: «What is the reason?» For «Jews the matter» of rendering the meat of the animal fit for consumption «is dependent upon» the performance of a valid act of «slaughter. Once there is full-fledged slaughter» and both simanim are cut, the innards «are permitted to them» even if the animal is convulsing. But with regard to «gentiles, for whom stabbing is sufficient» and slaughter is not required, the innards are permitted only after the animal is completely dead, since «the matter» of rendering the meat of the animal fit for consumption «is dependent upon» its «death.» Therefore, if the animal is still convulsing, «these» innards, which are considered to be outside the body after the cutting of the two simanim, are «considered like a limb from a living» animal and it is forbidden for gentiles to eat them.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הֲוָה יָתֵיבְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, וּבְעַי דְּאֵימָא לֵיהּ, מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דִּלְיִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁרֵי וּלְגוֹיִם אָסוּר? וְלָא אֲמַרִי לֵיהּ, דְּאָמֵינָא: הָא טַעְמָא קָאָמַר.
segments.en: «Rav Pappa said: I was sitting before Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov and I sought to say to him» that his statement is difficult: «Is there anything that is permitted for a Jew but prohibited for a gentile? But I did not say» that «to him, as I said» to myself: «Didn’t he say a reason» for his ruling? Therefore, there is no reason to ask the question.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא דְּלָא כְּרַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: הָרוֹצֶה לֶאֱכוֹל מִבְּהֵמָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ – חוֹתֵךְ כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר מִבֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה, וּמוֹלְחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וּמְדִיחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וּמַמְתִּין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ, וְאוֹכְלוֹ, אֶחָד גּוֹי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּתָּרִין בּוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «It is taught» in a baraita «not in accordance with» the opinion of «Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov: One who seeks to eat from» the meat of «an animal before its soul departs may cut an olive-bulk of meat from the area of the slaughter,» the neck, «and salt it very well,» i.e., more than is normally required, «and rinse it very well» in water to remove the salt and the blood, «and wait until the» animal’s «soul departs, and eat it.» It is «permitted» for «both a gentile and a Jew to» eat «it.» Contrary to the statement of Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov, there is no distinction between Jew and gentile.

segments.he: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין, דְּאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַשְׁיָאן: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיַּבְרִיא, חוֹתֵךְ כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר מִבֵּית שְׁחִיטָתָהּ שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה, וּמוֹלְחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וּמְדִיחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וּמַמְתִּין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ, אֶחָד גּוֹי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּתָּרִין בּוֹ.
segments.en: This baraita «supports» the statement of «Rav Idi bar Avin, as Rav Idi bar Avin says» that «Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashyan says: One who seeks to recuperate» from an illness should «cut an olive-bulk of meat from the area of slaughter,» i.e., the neck, «of an animal, and salt it very well, and rinse it very well, and wait until the» animal’s «soul departs,» and eat it. It is «permitted» for «both a gentile and a Jew to» eat «it.»

moves.cueHe: שחט את הוושט וכו׳
moves.summary: quotes the mishna's lemma, including that Rabbi Akiva conceded to Rabbi Yeshevav
moves.about: quoting the lemma of the mishna under discussion, that Rabbi Akiva conceded to Rabbi Yeshevav

moves.cueHe: ורמינהי
moves.summary: sets the Elu Tereifot mishna against our mishna
moves.about: whether a severed windpipe makes the animal a carcass (our mishna, after Rabbi Akiva's retraction) or a tereifa (Elu Tereifot)

moves.cueHe: נקובת הוושט ופסוקת הגרגרת
moves.summary: the contradicting text: a severed windpipe is listed as a tereifa
moves.about: the Elu Tereifot list, which counts a severed windpipe as a tereifa

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: לא קשיא, כאן ששחט ולבסוף פסק
moves.summary: Rava distinguishes by the order in which gullet and windpipe were cut
moves.about: the order of the cuts — gullet first then windpipe, versus windpipe first then gullet

moves.cueHe: איתיביה רב אחא בר הונא לרבא
moves.summary: objects from a baraita that rules both orders a carcass
moves.about: whether the order of cutting matters, against Rava's distinction

moves.cueHe: אימא: וכבר שחט את הוושט מעיקרא
moves.summary: Rava rereads the baraita's second case as one where the gullet had already been cut
moves.about: deflecting the baraita's objection to Rava's order-based distinction

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: שתי תשובות בדבר
moves.summary: defeats the rereading twice over: it duplicates the first case and deletes the words ואחר כך
moves.about: whether Rava's rereading of the baraita is tenable — it duplicates the first case and ignores the word ואחר כך

moves.cueHe: אלא אמר רבא: אלו אסורות קתני
moves.summary: Rava's replacement answer: the heading means 'these are forbidden', carcasses included
moves.about: resolving the contradiction by rereading אלו טרפות as a list of forbidden animals, not of tereifot only

moves.cueHe: וליחשוב נמי דחזקיה
moves.summary: then the list should also have counted Ḥizkiyya's and Rabbi Elazar's carcasses
moves.about: if the list includes carcasses, it should also have listed Ḥizkiyya's and Rabbi Elazar's carcass cases

moves.cueHe: כי קתני נבלה, דלא מטמאה מחיים
moves.summary: the list takes in only carcasses that do not impart impurity while alive
moves.about: the list teaches only carcasses that do not impart impurity while alive, which excludes Ḥizkiyya's and Rabbi Elazar's cases

moves.cueHe: רבי שמעון בן לקיש אמר: כאן – ששחט במקום חתך
moves.summary: Reish Lakish distinguishes by whether the gullet was cut at the place of the first cut
moves.about: whether the gullet was cut at the same place as the initial cut in the windpipe

moves.cueHe: ומי אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש הכי?
moves.summary: Reish Lakish's own lung ruling implies the severed windpipe is already 'in a basket'
moves.about: whether Reish Lakish can hold that slaughter still helps after the windpipe was severed, given his ruling about the lung placed 'in a basket'

moves.cueHe: אלא אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: in Rabbi Yoḥanan's name: the two mishnayot record Rabbi Akiva before and after his retraction
moves.about: the resolution that our mishna is after Rabbi Akiva's retraction and Elu Tereifot before it

moves.cueHe: גופא, אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש
moves.summary: returns to Reish Lakish's lung ruling to treat it for its own sake
moves.about: returning to Reish Lakish's lung ruling for its own sake

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: לא אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש אלא בריאה
moves.summary: Rava confines the leniency to the lung and denies it of the innards
moves.about: whether Reish Lakish's leniency extends past the lung to the innards

moves.cueHe: מתקיף לה רבי זירא
moves.summary: once signs of tereifa after slaughter began are permitted, lung and innards should be alike
moves.about: why lung and innards should differ once signs of tereifa arose after the slaughter had begun

moves.cueHe: והדר ביה רבי זירא
moves.summary: reports that Rabbi Zeira withdrew the objection
moves.about: his own objection to Rava's lung/innards distinction

moves.cueHe: דבעי רבי זירא: ניקבו בני מעיים בין סימן לסימן, מהו?
moves.summary: his dilemma: do the two simanim combine to purify from carcass impurity?
moves.about: whether the first siman joins with the second to purify the animal from carcass impurity when the innards were perforated between them

moves.cueHe: ואמרינן: לאו היינו דבעי אילפא
moves.summary: identifies Rabbi Zeira's dilemma with Ilfa's about a fetus extending its foreleg
moves.about: Ilfa's dilemma about a fetus that extended its foreleg between the cutting of the two simanim

moves.cueHe: מי מצטרף סימן ראשון לסימן שני לטהרה מידי נבלה, או לא?
moves.summary: spells out the shared dilemma of both cases
moves.about: spelling out that both dilemmas turn on whether the two cuts combine into one act of slaughter

moves.cueHe: עד כאן לא איבעיא לן, אלא לטהרה מידי נבלה
moves.summary: since only impurity was at issue and the meat is conceded forbidden, Rabbi Zeira did retract
moves.about: that Rabbi Zeira's dilemma concerns only impurity and concedes the meat is forbidden — proof he retracted his objection to Rava

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב אחא בר רב לרבינא: דלמא לעולם לא הדר ביה
moves.summary: perhaps he never retracted and argued only from Rava's own premise
moves.about: whether Rabbi Zeira in fact retracted, or only argued from Rava's own premise

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אחא בר יעקב: שמע מינה מדרבי שמעון בן לקיש
moves.summary: from Reish Lakish: innards may be offered to Jews but not to gentiles
moves.about: that innards may be offered to Jews but not to gentiles while the animal still convulses

moves.cueHe: מאי טעמא?
moves.summary: why should Jew and gentile differ?
moves.about: why Jews and gentiles should differ about the innards

moves.cueHe: ישראל דבשחיטה תליא מילתא
moves.summary: for Jews permission turns on slaughter, for gentiles on death, so to them the innards are a limb from a living animal
moves.about: for Jews permission depends on valid slaughter, for gentiles on the animal's death, so the innards are to them a limb from a living animal

moves.cueHe: אמר רב פפא: הוה יתיבנא קמיה דרב אחא בר יעקב
moves.summary: Rav Pappa reports the objection he formed before Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov and withheld, because a reason had been given
moves.about: Rav Pappa reporting that he sat as a disciple before Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov

moves.cueHe: תניא דלא כרב אחא בר יעקב
moves.summary: a baraita permits the meat to gentile and Jew alike, against his distinction
moves.about: a baraita permitting both gentile and Jew to eat meat cut from a still-living animal once salted, rinsed and held until it dies

moves.cueHe: מסייע ליה לרב אידי בר אבין
moves.summary: the same baraita supports Rav Idi bar Avin in Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashyan's name
moves.about: the same baraita supports Rav Idi bar Avin's ruling about cutting meat for one who seeks to recuperate
